analyst_view.overall: Promoted Racing (12th, 14 pts, most of them at home) host in-form Real Sociedad (5th, 22 pts) at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon; only Real Madrid have won there this season, and Racing won 2-1 at Málaga last time out. Racing miss Mantilla, Andrés Martín and Maguette Gueye (all in the numbers), Belocian is back and top scorer Zabiri is expected to lead the line. Real Sociedad's squad list leaves out Barrenetxea, Yangel Herrera and Odriozola (all in the numbers) and includes Mamadou Sarr, whom Matarazzo called an option to start; Kubo, Óskarsson and Oyarzabal are back from international duty, with Crystal Palace away in Europe on Thursday, and returning internationals such as Aramburu could start on the bench. Manuel Orellana referees; the numbers add a lot to cards for his record (5.9 a game).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and already take off Barrenetxea, Herrera, Andrés Martín and Gueye. Sarr's return at centre-back tightens Real Sociedad a little, while Racing's home games tend to be open with Íñigo Vicente and Zabiri; those pull both ways, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, already trimmed for Real Sociedad's lower recent corner count. Racing attack down the wings with Íñigo Vicente, Iker Luque and Pablo García, and Real Sociedad use Guedes and Kubo wide; nothing new changes that, so I keep 11.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, up sharply because referee Orellana (5.9 cards a game over 45 games) is counted, about +35%, on top of Racing's high recent card count (18 in six). Neither side has anyone suspended and the game has no derby or table edge, so with the referee already fully counted I stay at 7.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots and already add both sides' busy recent shooting (94 and 96 in six). Two open, attacking teams trading chances is what the numbers already show; Real Sociedad may start some returning internationals on the bench before Thursday's trip to Palace, but that is too uncertain to size, so 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Zabiri and Óskarsson, both scoring regularly, are expected to play, and Oyarzabal is back in the squad, as the numbers assume; no change, 10.4.
